hints: In right $\triangle ABC$, $\sin(\angle ABC) = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8 \implies \angle ABC \approx 0.9273\text{ rad}$.
walkthrough:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ (with right angle at $A$, opposite side $AC = 8\text{ cm}$ and hypotenuse $BC = 10\text{ cm}$):
$$\sin(\angle ABC) = \frac{AC}{BC} = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8$$
$$\angle ABC = \sin^{-1}(0.8) \approx 0.927295 \approx 0.9273\text{ radians} \quad (\text{to 4 s.f.})$$

hints: Sector $BCD$ area: $\frac{1}{2}(10^2)(2 \times 0.9273) \approx 92.73\text{ cm}^2 \implies$ segment area $\approx 44.73\text{ cm}^2$.
Semicircle area $32\pi \approx 100.53\text{ cm}^2$, subtract segment to find $55.8\text{ cm}^2$.
walkthrough:
Calculate $AB$ in $\triangle ABC$ using the Pythagorean theorem:
$$AB = \sqrt{BC^2 - AC^2} = \sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the area of triangle $\triangle BCD$ (base $CD = 16\text{ cm}$, height $AB = 6\text{ cm}$):
$$\text{Area}(\triangle BCD) = \frac{1}{2} \times CD \times AB = \frac{1}{2}(16)(6) = 48\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of circular sector $BCD$ (radius $10\text{ cm}$, angle $\angle CBD = 2(0.927295) = 1.85459\text{ rad}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } BCD) = \frac{1}{2}(10^2)(1.85459) = 50 \times 1.85459 = 92.7295\text{ cm}^2$$

Find the area of the circular segment of circle $B$ on chord $CD$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{segment } CD) = 92.7295 - 48 = 44.7295\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the shaded region by subtracting this segment from the semicircle of circle $A$ on diameter $CD$ (radius $8\text{ cm}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{semicircle } CAD) = \frac{1}{2}\pi(8^2) = 32\pi \approx 100.5310\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 32\pi - 44.7295 = 100.5310 - 44.7295 = 55.8015 \approx 55.8\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Shaded Composite Area: Finds $AB = 6$ and triangle area $48$ (M1, A1). Finds sector area $92.73$ (M1) and segment area $44.73$ (A1). Subtracts from semicircle $32\pi$ to get $55.8\text{ cm}^2$ (DM1, A1).
